what: GetDeps accepts an id equal to deps_.size() and then reads deps_[size], one element past the end.
why: A node whose id is exactly the size of deps_ (for instance the last id assigned, with no deps record) causes an out-of-bounds read and returns garbage as a Deps pointer.
note_must_say: GetDeps uses > instead of >= for the upper bound, so id == deps_.size() reads one past the end of deps_.
check: Scratch tree built with cmake and forge, g++ 13: exit 0, no compiler warning. ASan harness, RecordDeps(out, {in}) then GetDeps(in), whose id equals deps_.size(): pristine returns NULL; seeded heap-buffer-overflow in DepsLog::GetDeps (src/deps_log.cc:310).

what: RecomputeNodeDirty keeps the oldest input in most_recent_input: the comparison is reversed.
why: Output freshness is compared against the oldest input, so an output older than a newer input is considered clean and a stale artifact is not rebuilt. Compare the identical loop in Plan::CleanNode.
note_must_say: The most_recent_input comparison uses < instead of >, selecting the oldest input, so stale outputs are not detected as dirty.
check: Scratch tree built with cmake and forge, g++ 13: exit 0, no compiler warning. Build with two inputs, then only the newer one touched: pristine explains 'older than most recent input' and rebuilds; seeded 'no work to do'.

what: TopoSort::Visit searches a vector linearly to know whether an edge was already visited.
why: The membership test is called once per incoming edge of the graph, so the topological sort degrades to O(E^2); the comment above still says a simple set is used. The order and the result are unchanged.
note_must_say: TopoSort uses a linear std::find over a vector as its visited set, making ComputeCriticalPath quadratic in the number of edges.
check: Scratch tree built with cmake and forge, g++ 13: exit 0, no compiler warning. forge's own ComputeCriticalPath metric (-n -d stats, Debug build, independent edges) at 5000/10000/20000/40000 edges: 1.6/3.0/8.1/12.0 ms on pristine, 51.4/204.9/811.8/3269.6 ms on seeded, about 4x per doubling. Same [N/N] edge count reported by the dry run on 40000 edges.

what: Subprocess::Finish repeats the waitpid loop of TryFinish instead of calling it.
why: The reaping logic, including EINTR handling and the exit-status translation, now has two copies that can diverge.
note_must_say: Subprocess::Finish duplicates the waitpid/EINTR loop of TryFinish instead of calling it.
check: Scratch tree built with cmake and forge, g++ 13: exit 0, no compiler warning. A failing command (exit 3) and a console-pool job give output and exit status identical to pristine.

what: In SpellcheckNode the variable tracking the smallest distance seen is named max_distance.
why: The name states the opposite of the value it holds and reads as a maximum alongside kMaxValidEditDistance, misleading anyone tuning the suggestion threshold.
note_must_say: SpellcheckNode's max_distance actually tracks the minimum distance so far; the name says the opposite.
check: Scratch tree built with cmake and forge, g++ 13: exit 0, no compiler warning. Rename of one local, reasoned. `forge -n target_on` gives the same 'did you mean' as pristine.

what: ParseDefault was rewritten as a single counted loop of if/else chains with comma operators, assignments in conditions and one-letter names.
why: The grammar it implements (at least one target, then more, then newline) is no longer visible; the error for the first empty path depends on a loop counter hidden in a comma expression.
note_must_say: ParseDefault is rewritten as an unreadable counter loop with comma operators, assignments in conditions and one-letter names.
check: Scratch tree built with cmake and forge, g++ 13: exit 0, no compiler warning. Manifests with valid `default a b` and with four malformed or edge forms (no target, unknown target, empty variable): output and exit status identical to pristine.

what: disk_interface.cc now includes graph.h and calls Node::PathDecanonicalized from DirName.
why: The disk abstraction is below the build graph (graph.cc includes disk_interface.h and calls DiskInterface). The lowest layer now depends on the graph layer for a call that, with slash_bits 0, is an identity.
note_must_say: disk_interface.cc includes graph.h and calls Node::PathDecanonicalized: the disk layer depends upward on the build graph.
check: Scratch tree built with cmake and forge, g++ 13: exit 0, no compiler warning. Links with graph.o. Harness including disk_interface.cc dumped DirName for all 511 strings over {a,/} up to length 8: identical to pristine.

what: DepsLog::Load no longer checks the record size read from the file before fread into a fixed stack buffer.
why: buf is kMaxRecordSize + 1 bytes on the stack and size comes from the log file. A corrupted or crafted .forge_deps file overflows the stack buffer.
note_must_say: The size > kMaxRecordSize check was removed, so a record size from the file overflows the fixed stack buffer buf in fread.
check: Scratch tree built with cmake and forge, g++ 13: exit 0, no compiler warning. A .forge_deps with a record header announcing 2 MiB, followed by 2 MiB: pristine 'premature end of file; recovering', exit 0; seeded SIGSEGV, exit 139.

what: SIGCHLD is no longer blocked outside ppoll/pselect.
why: The comment says handlers are only enabled during ppoll/pselect. A child exiting while the signal is unblocked runs the handler, then DoWork resets s_sigchld_received to 0 and enters ppoll: the wakeup is lost and a console subprocess, which has no pipe, is never reaped, so the build hangs.
note_must_say: SIGCHLD is left unblocked outside ppoll, so an early child exit is lost when DoWork clears s_sigchld_received: signal race and possible hang for console jobs.
check: Scratch tree built with cmake and forge, g++ 13: exit 0, no compiler warning. Harness: Add a console 'true', sleep 300 ms so the child exits before DoWork, then loop on DoWork: pristine reaps it, exit 0; seeded never reaps it and was killed by the 5 s timeout (137).

new:
if (errno == ENOENT || errno == ENOTDIR || errno == EACCES)
      return 0;
what: RealDiskInterface::Stat treats a permission error as 'file does not exist'.
why: Stat's return of 0 means missing. An unreadable directory now produces a plausible 'missing' answer instead of an error, so forge reports a missing input or rebuilds and overwrites outputs instead of stopping.
note_must_say: Stat maps EACCES to 0 (missing) instead of reporting the error, converting a permission failure into a false 'file does not exist'.
check: Scratch tree built with cmake and forge, g++ 13: exit 0, no compiler warning. Input inside a directory with mode 000, run as non-root: pristine 'stat(sub/in): Permission denied'; seeded "'sub/in', needed by 'out', missing and no known rule to make it".

what: LoadDepFile keeps the not-found message in *err instead of clearing it.
why: The comments promise 'Treat a missing depfile as empty' and 'On a missing depfile: return false and empty *err'. RecomputeNodeDirty aborts when *err is non-empty, so a missing depfile now fails the build instead of forcing a rebuild.
note_must_say: LoadDepFile no longer clears *err for NotFound, breaking its documented 'missing depfile returns false with empty *err' behaviour.
check: Scratch tree built with cmake and forge, g++ 13: exit 0, no compiler warning. Rule with a depfile that the command does not write: pristine builds, exit 0; seeded 'forge: error: No such file or directory', exit 1.

what: BuildLog::Load returns on the invalid-version path without closing the file it opened.
why: Every other exit from Load closes file; here the FILE and its descriptor leak, and on Windows the unlink of the still-open file fails.
note_must_say: The invalid-log-version branch of BuildLog::Load returns without fclose(file), leaking the FILE.
check: Scratch tree built with cmake and forge, g++ 13: exit 0, no compiler warning. Harness calling BuildLog::Load on a '# forge log v1' file, counting /proc/self/fd: delta 0 on pristine, 1 on seeded.
